newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine govt unhappy with 1997 privatisation plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine govt unhappy with 1997 privatisation plan.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has sharply criticised the state privatisation agency's 1997 plan for not guaranteeing significant injections of foreign investment into the economy, the government's press service said on Friday.
"The Prime Minister (Pavlo Lazarenko) and other government members gave the State Property Fund (FDM) plan a very low grade," a statement said.
It quoted Lazarenko as saying the plan showed an "errant privatisation ideology" by not backing increased investment and said he ordered the Fund to submit a second document.
Ukraine has attracted only about $1.2 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991. It has also been criticised for the slow pace of privatisation.
Fund chairman Yuri Yekhanurov said previously that the agency plans to sell more than 70 percent of shares in 3,000 large and medium-size enterprises. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
